check: whether running test and runGameTest in one gradle invocation is safe, since step 3 depends on it and the wrong answer costs three and a half hours
why: Step 3 was changed to run both tasks because they are independent - runGameTest writes only the gametest report while test produces the JUnit XML that step 4 archives. If invoking them together caused a conflict, the failure would appear deep into a multi-hour run.

theTaskGraphIsCoherent.order: compileJava through testClasspathBridge and test, then compileGametestJava through gametestClasses and runGameTest
theTaskGraphIsCoherent.sharedPrerequisites: Five compile tasks appear once each, so Gradle deduplicates them rather than building twice

outputsDoNotCollide.verdict: No shared path, so neither can overwrite the other's results

aFlagThatLookedAlarmingAndIsNot.observation: gradle.properties sets org.gradle.parallel=true, which would suggest the two tasks could run concurrently if they were independent
aFlagThatLookedAlarmingAndIsNot.whyItIsInert: Gradle's parallel flag parallelises execution across projects. settings.gradle declares only rootProject.name, and no subdirectory holds a build.gradle, so this is a single-project build with nothing to parallelise across.
aFlagThatLookedAlarmingAndIsNot.additionalReassurance: Even if they did run concurrently, their output paths are disjoint, so neither writes what the other reads.

conclusion: Invoking gradlew test runGameTest together is safe, and step 3 keeps both tasks.
